label: The vanishing apprenticeship
title: If AI does the junior work, where do seniors come from?
thesis: The tasks that historically taught new software engineers their judgement — small fixes, boilerplate, reading unfamiliar code slowly — are the tasks machines now absorb first. If entry to the profession stops running through that work, the field must either find another way to manufacture senior judgement or accept a narrowing pipeline into it. Evidence currently points in both directions, which is itself the finding.
currentPressure: Entry-level postings and internships have fallen sharply while overall engineering demand has not, so the contraction is concentrated at the point where the profession recruits.

implications.statement: The entry point to software work moves from doing simple tasks towards supervising machine output, a job that assumes judgement newcomers have not yet built.
Skill formation must be deliberately designed rather than acquired as a by-product of routine work.
Newcomers are evaluated on output they did not produce and may not fully understand, which unsettles what it means to be competent early in a career.

evidence.note: Seoul National University field interviews argue AI has absorbed the traditional apprenticeship work
assistants lift seniors while making it harder for juniors to build engineering judgement
randomised trial: a two-minute speed-up correlated with a 17% drop in learning
67% fall in entry-level postings; 7.7% junior employment decline at AI-adopting firms
comprehension debt: the gap between code that exists and code anyone understands

Randomised trial, 52 mostly junior engineers learning an unfamiliar library: the AI-assisted group scored 50% against 67% on a follow-up comprehension quiz, with the largest gap on debugging questions. Measures whether the learner acquires the judgement, not how fast the task finished.

Interviews with thirteen interns and junior developers: they describe shallow learning that makes the critical judgement the market now asks of them harder to build, and identify AI dependence in peers while rejecting it in themselves.

900+ developer survey: senior engineers report using AI instead of mentoring juniors, and less experienced developers spend more tokens on unproductive work. Measures the transmission route into senior judgement, not the labour market around it.

Observed-exposure metric ranks computer programmers the most exposed occupation, finds no statistically meaningful rise in unemployment for exposed workers, and only suggestive evidence that hiring has slowed for younger entrants into exposed occupations. The pipeline is measured; the direction is unsettled.

Anthropic workforce data: junior share of technical hires 27% to 9%, of technical headcount 21% to 14%, while technical hiring still grew; authors say it is one fast-growing AI lab and the cause is not explained
CNN: software engineering job openings rebound on AI project demand; aggregate demand, not junior entry, so context for the composition-effect reading rather than counter-evidence
SignalFire: engineering the most resilient job function; aggregate demand, not junior entry, so context for the composition-effect reading rather than counter-evidence

reachRationale: The contraction in entry-level hiring is visible across independent labour-market datasets rather than at individual employers, and the learning mechanism now has field evidence behind it — but aggregate engineering demand has held up, so this has not become a settled change in how the profession recruits.
whatWouldChangeThis: Entry-level postings recover to their 2023 share of engineering hiring and hold for two quarters
Cohorts entering through AI-supervision roles reach senior-level judgement on the same timescale as earlier cohorts

developmentPaths.title: Apprenticeship gets designed
developmentPaths.description: Employers and educators build deliberate skill-formation paths to replace what routine work used to teach.

developmentPaths.title: The pipeline narrows
developmentPaths.description: Entry stays scarce, seniority becomes a scarce and expensive asset, and the field ages.

developmentPaths.title: Supervision becomes the entry role
developmentPaths.description: Newcomers start by directing and checking machine output, and judgement forms differently rather than not at all.

construct: Whether the routes by which new software engineers build judgement are narrowing — entry-level hiring, the work juniors are given, and what juniors learn when machines do it first. Not overall engineering demand, total layoffs, or the share of developers using AI, which move without any change in how juniors enter or learn the profession.
